citation: Cooper et al. (2026), A dataset of rated conceptual arguments
title: A dataset of rated conceptual arguments
authors: Emery Cooper; Caspar Oesterheld; Linh Chi Nguyen; Alexander Kastner; Ethan Perez
task_description: Benchmark models judge contextualized critiques of conceptual positions rather than settle a final philosophical answer.
inputs: 442 position texts and 951 argumentative critiques in the arXiv version; expert ratings across conceptual topics.
outputs_or_labels: Expert ratings for centrality, strength, correctness, clarity, dead weight, single-issue focus, and overall quality; two scoring functions and model ranking.
pipeline_gap_filled: expert evaluation of objection/critique quality; multi-dimensional philosophical argument scoring
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF and dataset PDF found; runnable artifact packaging not independently verified
evidence_basis: ArXiv abstract states 951 critiques, 442 positions, 1,458 ratings by six experts; official dataset PDF provides method context. Current LMCA webpage reports a later version with 560 positions, 1,461 arguments, and 2,140 ratings; version drift is preserved, not merged.
limitations: Judges individual critiques, not a complete quaestio with sed contra, respondeo, distinctions, and one-to-one replies; source/style confounds and version drift require pinning.
why_relevant: Closest found resource for expert-scored philosophical objections and replies as contextualized arguments; supplies rubrics for strength, correctness, relevance/centrality, and clarity.

title: DebateQA: Evaluating Question Answering on Debatable Knowledge
authors: Rongwu Xu; Xuan Qi; Zehan Qi; Wei Xu; Zhijiang Guo
task_description: Evaluates answers to inherently debatable questions where a single fixed answer is inadequate.
inputs: 2,941 debatable questions, each paired with multiple human-annotated partial answers representing perspectives.
outputs_or_labels: Perspective Diversity and Dispute Awareness metrics; human preference alignment and model/RAG comparisons.
pipeline_gap_filled: complete-answer coverage of competing perspectives and explicit recognition of contestability
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF verified; dataset artifact URL not located in the inspected record
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/PDF explicitly states 2,941 questions, multiple partial answers, and the two metrics.
limitations: No typed objection, authority, determination, distinction, or reply alignment; perspective coverage is broader but shallower than scholastic obligations.
why_relevant: Best current benchmark for answer-level debatable-issue coverage; useful outer-loop metric for whether a rendered disputation acknowledges and covers competing positions.

citation: Sanayei et al. (2025), Can LLMs Judge Debates?
title: Can LLMs Judge Debates? Evaluating Non-Linear Reasoning via Argumentation Theory Semantics
authors: Reza Sanayei; Srdjan Vesic; Eduardo Blanco; Mihai Surdeanu
task_description: Tests whether LLMs can infer argument acceptability rankings from dialogue-formatted debates with latent attack/support graphs.
inputs: 325 arguments and 303 relations from 12AngryMen and DebatePedia NoDE datasets; graph edges hidden from models.
outputs_or_labels: Rank correlation/alignment with QuAD semantics under prompting strategies; length and discourse-order robustness analysis.
pipeline_gap_filled: structured debate graph evaluation and non-linear acceptability of arguments
authenticity_class: human-curated debate graphs with formal semantics
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF verified; underlying NoDE artifact not separately checked in this pass
evidence_basis: ACL abstract and PDF state latent graph construction, QuAD ranking gold, 325 arguments/303 relations, and degradation with longer/disrupted inputs.
limitations: Does not evaluate generated complete disputations or scholastic stages; QuAD acceptability is not historical authority or philosophical truth.
why_relevant: Directly reusable graph-level evaluator for objection/reply networks and a warning against linear-only judging.

title: SocREval: Large Language Models with the Socratic Method for Reference-free Reasoning Evaluation
authors: Hangfeng He; Hongming Zhang; Dan Roth
task_description: Uses Socratic-style evaluator prompting to assess generated reasoning chains without a gold chain.
inputs: Model-produced reasoning chains evaluated on four human-annotated reasoning datasets.
outputs_or_labels: Reference-free quality scores using Definition, Maieutics, and Dialectic prompting; correlation/benchmark comparison against ROSCOE and ReCEval.
pipeline_gap_filled: reference-free evaluation of intermediate reasoning quality and evaluator interrogation
authenticity_class: human-annotated reasoning datasets; generated evaluator outputs
artifact_access_status: code repository linked from official PDF; dataset artifacts inherited from four prior datasets
license_status: code license/artifact terms not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/PDF reports four human-annotated datasets, GPT-4 evaluator, and comparisons with reference-free/reference-based metrics.
limitations: Evaluator is a prompted judge and not a validated scholastic rubric; no authority, distinction, or reply-to-objection labels.
why_relevant: Provides a concrete method for stage-by-stage evaluator questioning and a baseline for testing whether LLM judges track expert disputation judgments.

title: MARS: Benchmarking the Metaphysical Reasoning Abilities of Language Models with a Multi-task Evaluation Dataset
task_description: Philosophy-specific multi-task benchmark for reasoning about action changes, state changes, and situational transitions.
outputs_or_labels: Three task labels corresponding to plausibility of action changes, caused state changes, and situational transitions; evaluates 20 models.
pipeline_gap_filled: philosophy-domain reasoning control and distinction/transition sensitivity
authenticity_class: constructed benchmark with public code/data claim in abstract
artifact_access_status: official GitHub artifact link stated in arXiv abstract; artifact contents/license not independently inspected
evidence_basis: arXiv abstract explicitly defines the three tasks, evaluates 20 LLMs, and links public data/models.
limitations: Discriminative transition reasoning, not complete generated argumentation; no objection coverage, authority, or reply scoring.
why_relevant: Useful domain control for whether a disputation preserves metaphysical distinctions and transition conditions rather than merely sounding philosophical.

title: Mining Complex Patterns of Argumentative Reasoning in Natural Language Dialogue
authors: Ramon Ruiz-Dolz; Zlata Kikteva; John Lawrence
task_description: Evaluates mining of fine-grained argumentation schemes in natural-language dialogue.
outputs_or_labels: Scheme labels and LLM/Transformer classification results.
pipeline_gap_filled: typed objection/reply form recognition; upstream structural labels
authenticity_class: dialogue arguments with human scheme annotations
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF verified; corpus download not independently located
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states 441 arguments and 24 schemes and describes LLM/Transformer validation on real-world dialogue.
limitations: Argument-scheme classification is component-level, not complete disputation generation or end-to-end faithfulness.
why_relevant: Strongest current representation precedent for typed form labels that can underwrite scholastic objection, distinction, and reply categories.

title: Can Large Language Models Understand Argument Schemes?
authors: Elfia Bezou-Vrakatseli; Oana Cocarascu; Sanjay Modgil
task_description: Systematically evaluates LLM classification of Walton argument schemes under zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting.
inputs: Manually annotated and automatically generated arguments, including enthymemes.
outputs_or_labels: Scheme classification accuracy across seven LLMs and prompting/instruction strategies.
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF verified; exact dataset package not independently located
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states seven LLMs, manual/generated arguments, enthymemes, and Walton taxonomy.
limitations: Does not generate or score a complete disputation; generated items weaken authenticity for some analyses.
why_relevant: Useful classifier baseline and failure test for whether a scholastic engine correctly identifies objection/reply inferential forms.

title: Socratic Question Generation: A Novel Dataset, Models, and Evaluation
authors: Beng Heng Ang; Sujatha Das Gollapalli; See-Kiong Ng
task_description: Benchmarks generation of type-sensitive Socratic questions that elicit reasoning and alternate views from a context.
inputs: 110K question-context pairs; 105K labeled pairs used for train/dev/test in the paper.
outputs_or_labels: Question-type labels; BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, BERTScore/BLEURT, and human evaluation.
authenticity_class: large human-origin question/context corpus (Reddit-derived per paper context)
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF verified; artifact access not independently checked
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/PDF states 110K pairs, question types, automated and human evaluation, and low n-gram overlap due to legitimate question diversity.
limitations: Only the questioning stage; no answer determination, authority, or replies.
why_relevant: A practical source for evaluating whether generated objections are relevant, type-appropriate, and non-redundant before rendering a full quaestio.

title: Evaluating large language models’ ability to generate interpretive arguments
task_description: Collects human and model-generated arguments for and against interpretations of ambiguous rules/scenarios and evaluates quality/persuasiveness.
inputs: Professional-ethics rules plus ambiguous scenarios involving open-textured phrases; human and LLM arguments.
outputs_or_labels: Human ratings of quality/persuasiveness and human-vs-machine discrimination study.
pipeline_gap_filled: attack/support generation and expert/human evaluation of interpretive argument quality
authenticity_class: human-authored rules/scenarios plus human and model arguments
artifact_access_status: open-access paper/PDF verified; underlying dataset not independently located
license_status: CC BY-NC 4.0 stated on official page
evidence_basis: Official SAGE abstract states curated rules/scenarios, collected human/LLM arguments, quality/persuasiveness evaluation, and Turing-style study.
limitations: Legal/ethical interpretation rather than scholastic philosophy; persuasive quality is not validity, authority fidelity, or reply alignment.
why_relevant: Closest empirical precedent for evaluating generated arguments on both sides of an interpretive issue with human quality judgments.

title: R ESEARCH QA: Evaluating Scholarly Question Answering at Scale Across 75 Fields with Survey-Mined Questions and Rubrics
authors: Li S. Yifei; Allen Chang; Chaitanya Malaviya; Mark Yatskar
task_description: Evaluates scholarly answers using survey-mined questions and explicit rubrics across many fields.
inputs: 7.6K head-to-head evaluations over 75 fields; scholarly questions with rubric items.
outputs_or_labels: Rubric-item coverage, including citation, limitation, and comparison items; system pairwise evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: complete scholarly-output rubric coverage, citations, limitations, and comparisons
authenticity_class: survey-mined scholarly questions with human rubric construction
artifact_access_status: paper/PDF verified; dataset artifact not independently inspected
evidence_basis: ACL record states 18 systems, 7.6K head-to-heads, rubric coverage results, and release of data.
limitations: Not specifically philosophical or dialectical; rubric items do not guarantee objection/reply structure.
why_relevant: Useful outer-loop evaluator for complete answers: checks whether a scholastic output covers citations, limitations, comparisons, and all requested components.

title: Semantic-Aware Logical Reasoning via a Semiotic Framework
authors: Authors listed on ACL record as Zhang et al.
task_description: Benchmark of abstract propositions with systematically constructed contrary and contradictory forms, derived from philosophical reasoning settings.
inputs: Abstract propositions and contrary/contradictory variants; benchmark instances and logic tasks.
outputs_or_labels: Logical correctness judgments and performance on RepublicQA plus four other logic benchmarks.
pipeline_gap_filled: contrary/contradictory stance control and philosophical logic robustness
authenticity_class: systematically constructed propositions; authenticity lower than historical disputation
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF verified; official artifact not independently located
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states RepublicQA, abstract propositions, contrary/contradictory forms, and cross-benchmark results. An OpenReview artifact record describes derivation from Plato’s Republic but is not used as sole evidence.
limitations: No generated complete disputation, provenance, authority, distinction, or reply metrics.
why_relevant: Good symbolic control for contradiction/contrary handling, but not an output benchmark for scholastic form.

title: Can LLMs Judge Debates? Evaluating Non-Linear Reasoning via Argumentation Theory Semantics
authors: Reza Sanayei; Srdjan Vesic; Eduardo Blanco; Mihai Surdeanu
benchmark_or_resource_name: NoDE debate graphs with QuAD semantics
task_description: Duplicate/version-family record intentionally preserved? No: this is a screening note showing the same paper should not be counted twice.
inputs: dialogue debates and latent argument graphs
evidence_basis: Search returned the same official ACL paper/PDF in multiple URL forms; deduplication rule keeps one benchmark record.
why_relevant: Preserves a failed duplicate search and prevents inflated counts.

citation: Uckelman (2013), medieval obligationes as formal dialogue systems
title: Medieval Disputationes de obligationibus as Formal Dialogue Systems
task_description: Formalizes a medieval dialogue protocol with Opponent/Respondent roles, legal moves, and consistency outcomes; it is not an empirical benchmark.
inputs: Medieval obligationes propositions and protocol states.
outputs_or_labels: Formal dialogue semantics and legal response rules.
pipeline_gap_filled: historical protocol model, not benchmark evaluation
artifact_access_status: article page verified in local retained review; no benchmark artifact
evidence_basis: Local retained source `agents/23_disputatio_dialectical_ai.md` records the opened Springer article and its exact protocol overlap.
limitations: No model-output benchmark, expert rubric, or complete scholastic quaestio evaluation.
why_relevant: Critical protocol precedent, but must not be reported as a benchmark.

title: PhilosophyBench
authors: Stanford University research study; named advisors on official site
task_description: Independent study intended to evaluate AI-written philosophy with statistically validated human methodology.
inputs: AI-generated English-language philosophical essays and participant-written/evaluated philosophy tasks; exact public benchmark package not frozen.
outputs_or_labels: Planned human ratings of originality, clarity, depth, sophistication, and related philosophical writing qualities.
pipeline_gap_filled: complete philosophical output evaluation, but not yet a frozen scholarly benchmark artifact
authenticity_class: human expert study design; public artifact status not frozen
artifact_access_status: official site is accessible, but study data/benchmark and final methods are not yet released in inspected record
license_status: study privacy/IRB constraints; reuse restrictions explicit on official site
evidence_basis: Official site states Stanford IRB-approved independent study and aims to evaluate AI philosophical writing; FAQ says autograder reliability is not assumed.
limitations: Not specifically disputation-shaped; study is active and not a reproducible released benchmark as of the search date.
why_relevant: Important watch item for complete philosophical outputs and human rubrics; do not treat as runnable benchmark until methods/artifacts freeze.
